cards.text: Out in Israel's camp, there's the son of an Israelite mother and an Egyptian father. He goes out among the Israelites, and a fight breaks out between him and an Israelite man. The text never says what the fight was about, and I'm not about to make it up.

cards.question: In the middle of that fight, what does the son of the Israelite woman do?

answers.text: He knocks the man to the ground
He runs off from the camp

cards.text: So they bring him to Moses, Israel's leader. And right here the text stops to name his mother: Shelomith daughter of Dibri.

cards.question: Shelomith daughter of Dibri, the blasphemer's mother, is from which tribe of Israel?

cards.text: Moses has a man in front of him who blasphemed the Name, and nobody rushes this one. I respect that, friend, because I rushed a batch once and pulled out cookies you could SKIP across a lake.

cards.question: While they wait, what do they do with the blasphemer?

answers.text: They send him back to his tent
They hand him over to his family

cards.question: They hold the blasphemer until the will of the ___ is made clear to them.

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Moses. First thing: take the blasphemer outside the camp.

cards.question: Outside the camp, who does the LORD say lays their hands on the blasphemer's head?
And who does the LORD say is to stone the blasphemer?

answers.text: The men of the tribe of Dan

cards.text: But the LORD isn't done. He gives Moses a law for all the Israelites: anyone who curses his God bears the consequences of his sin, and whoever blasphemes the name of the LORD must surely be put to death, stoned by the whole assembly.

cards.question: The LORD says the law against blaspheming His name covers native Israelites but not foreign residents.

cards.text: Then the law moves from words to actions. If a man takes the life of anyone else, he must surely be put to death.

cards.question: What if someone kills an animal instead of a person? What does the LORD say he must do?

cards.text: Next the LORD covers what happens when someone injures his neighbor. Get ready, friend, because you've heard this next line before, even if you never knew where it came from.

cards.question: Fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. What's the idea behind that rule?

answers.text: The penalty is twice the injury
The injured man names the penalty

cards.text: Then the LORD sets the two cases side by side. Whoever kills an animal must make restitution, but whoever kills a man must be put to death.

cards.question: To close, the LORD says who gets the same standard of law. Who is it?

answers.text: The foreign resident and the native

cards.question: What reason does the LORD give for one standard of law for everyone?

answers.text: He is the LORD their God
The tribes asked Him for it
Moses could not judge each case

cards.question: Moses speaks to the Israelites, and they take the blasphemer outside the camp and stone him, just as the LORD commanded Moses.

findings.problem: Multiple choice takes 9 of the 12 choice cards (2, 4, 6, 9, 10, 14, 16, 18, 19). There are only 2 true or false cards and 1 fill in the blank card, so one type dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: "In the middle of that fight" says when the blasphemy happened. Verses 10 and 11 tell the fight and then the blasphemy, but they never say the blasphemy happened during the fight. The question adds a time and a connection the text leaves open. Something like "Then the son of the Israelite woman does something. What is it?" would keep it open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The mother's tribe is a side note in a parenthesis. It doesn't move the passage forward, and the baker doesn't need it to understand the passage. It is also a pure luck guess. Card 3 already names her, so the tribe can simply be told there.

rule.text: Ask about the moments that move the passage forward and the details the baker needs to understand it.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't click. Rushing a batch usually gives soft, underbaked cookies, not rock-hard ones you could skip across a lake, so the cause and the result don't fit together and a stranger would say "huh?". Also, a stone-skipping image right before a man is stoned to death sits uneasily.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining. If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: "You've heard this next line before" assumes something about this baker that Papa Dorin hasn't been told. "Even if you never knew where it came from" also suggests the line starts here, but it appears earlier, in Exodus 21:24.

rule.text: What he doesn't know: anything about the individual baker that he hasn't been told, such as their streak, their mood, the time of day or how they've done before. In lessons, he's never told, because every baker gets the same lesson.
